Model United Nations · Advanced level

MUN Journal Writing Book

A 67-page journal I wrote for Taiwanese students who had never heard of Model United Nations. It does not start with debate rules. It starts with ideas students can connect to, then adds the vocabulary, and only then moves to MUN itself.

  1. Unlock the words firstWord scrambles and definitions for words like principle, organization and values before any reading.
  2. Human rightsStudents explore their own rights as students and link them to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
  3. The United NationsIts four goals, the 193 member flags, and how the General Assembly, Security Council and other bodies work.
  4. Why the UN mattersPicture prompts and real news articles that students summarize in their own journal entries.
  5. My MUN adventureChinese support for key ideas, then position papers, debate and negotiation.

Wonders · Grade 6 · Unit 4

Planning a story lesson: A Telephone Mix-Up

My reading lessons follow the Wonders story page by page. I plan them as one screen per step so the class always knows where we are, and I put the student picker right next to every question.

Warm-up · slide 1 of 12

How I planned it

Twelve short steps, in the order the class meets them.

  1. Warm-up and essential questionStudents connect the unit question to their own morning before opening the book.
  2. Key words firstNew vocabulary with meanings and a quick check, so the story is readable.
  3. Genre and story elementsWhat makes it historical fiction, then characters, setting, problem and resolution on one screen.
  4. Close reading, one page at a timePages 45 to 47 each get "what the author wants us to understand", text evidence to box, underline or circle, and check questions. On page 45, students see how a new invention divides a town: some people welcome change and some fear it.
  5. Skills, response and exit ticketPoint of view, predictions and synonyms, then a written response and a short exit ticket.
The picker beside every question. Each question has its own Ring button, and a Ring a student bar sits at the bottom of every slide. It picks a name at random and keeps count of who has answered, so every student gets a turn.
Elementary Science Coordinator · Victoria Academy

New ideas that make class fun

I keep lessons lively by bringing in something new: a spinning wheel, a race, a game built around the day's topic. As Elementary Science Coordinator, I also build tools the whole science department uses, from Grade 1 to Grade 6.
